name: ADP7142AUJZ-R7
title: 40 V, 200 mA low-noise CMOS LDO regulator
summary: A CMOS linear regulator that takes 2.7 V to 40 V in and delivers up to 200 mA, with 11 µV rms output noise and 88 dB PSRR at 10 kHz. It comes as an adjustable part (1.2 V reference) and in fixed outputs from 1.2 V to 5.0 V, any of which can be raised with a divider on SENSE/ADJ. It is stable with a 2.2 µF ceramic output capacitor, has a precision enable with hysteresis, current limit and thermal shutdown, and soft start set by a capacitor on the LFCSP and SOIC. Packages are a 2 mm × 2 mm 6-lead LFCSP, an 8-lead SOIC with exposed pad and a 5-lead TSOT; ADP7142AUJZ-R7 is the adjustable TSOT.

circuits.title: Fixed 5 V output
circuits.description: A 5 V fixed-output part fed from 6 V. SENSE/ADJ is tied straight to the output node. 2.2 µF ceramics decouple input and output, and a 1 nF capacitor on SS stretches the start-up ramp. EN is driven by an on/off control.

circuits.title: 5 V part set to 6 V
circuits.description: A 5 V fixed-output part raised to 6 V by a divider on SENSE/ADJ: 2 kΩ from the output to the pin and 10 kΩ from the pin to ground, so VOUT = 5 V × (1 + 2 k/10 k). Input is 7 V, with 2.2 µF on each side, 1 nF on SS and EN on an on/off control.

circuits.title: EN pin voltage divider
circuits.description: The on/off control reaches EN through 200 kΩ, with 100 kΩ from EN to ground, so the part turns on at 3.6 V on the control line with 300 mV of hysteresis instead of at the 1.2 V threshold. Input is 8 V, the output is marked 6 V, and SENSE/ADJ sits on a divider of 10 kΩ (R1, from VOUT) and 20 kΩ (R2, to ground); 2.2 µF decouples each side. SS is not connected.
notes: R3 is REN1 and R4 is REN2 in the enable equations.

circuits.title: 12 V output with noise reduction network
circuits.description: A 5 V part set to 12 V from a 14 V input by 91 kΩ (R1) and 10 kΩ (R2) on SENSE/ADJ. A 1 µF capacitor in series with 1 kΩ sits across R1, so above a few hertz the error amplifier runs near unity gain and the output noise stays close to that of a fixed part. EN is driven from the on/off control through a 200 kΩ / 100 kΩ divider. 2.2 µF decouples each side.
notes: R3 is RNR and C3 is CNR in the noise equations. No SS connection is used.

equations.note: The ground-current term is small and can be dropped, giving TJ = TA + {[(VIN − VOUT) × ILOAD] × θJA}.

operation.text: Inside are a PMOS pass transistor, an error amplifier and a voltage reference. The amplifier compares the reference with the fed-back output and drives the PMOS gate down to raise the output or up to lower it. Quiescent current is 180 µA typical at full load and shutdown current is under 3 µA at room temperature.

Fifteen factory output voltages from 1.2 V to 5.0 V. Any fixed part can be raised above its factory voltage with a divider on SENSE/ADJ, giving outputs from 1.2 V up to VIN − VDO. Output noise is 11 µV rms regardless of setting for fixed parts of 5 V or less.

VOUT turns on when a rising EN crosses about 1.2 V and off when a falling EN crosses about 1.1 V; the 100 mV hysteresis keeps noise on EN from making the output chatter. A divider from the supply to EN raises both thresholds.

With SS open an internal ramp limits inrush; the 3.3 V option reaches 90 % of its final value about 380 µs after EN crosses its threshold, and the time depends on the output setting. A capacitor from SS to GND lengthens the ramp. SS exists only on the LFCSP and SOIC and must not be grounded.

The low noise comes from running the error amplifier at unity gain with the reference equal to the output. Raising the output with a divider scales the noise with the gain, so a factory voltage close to the target keeps noise down. A capacitor CNR in series with RNR across R1 lowers the AC gain: with RNR 1 % to 10 % of R2 the minimum AC gain is about 0.1 dB to 0.8 dB, and CNR is chosen so its reactance equals R1 − RNR somewhere between 1 Hz and 50 Hz. In the 12 V example (DC gain 10, 20 dB; roll-off 1.75 Hz; HF gain 1.099, 0.82 dB) noise falls from 70 µV rms to 12 µV rms, about 15.3 dB against a theoretical 19.2 dB. Above about 40 kHz the amplifier's open-loop gain limits closed-loop gain, which is why 70 µV rms is measured rather than the 110 µV rms the DC gain implies.
The noise reduction network adds a pole to the feedback loop and slows start-up; this matters where supplies must come up in sequence.

Small ceramic capacitors are the intended choice; other types work if their ESR is low enough. At least 2.2 µF with ESR of 0.3 Ω or less keeps the loop stable. More output capacitance improves the response to large load steps.
2.2 µF from VIN to GND makes the circuit less sensitive to layout, long input traces and source impedance. When more than 2.2 µF is used on the output, the input capacitor should be raised to match.

X5R or X7R rated 6.3 V to 100 V are recommended; Y5V and Z5U are not, for their temperature and bias behaviour. X5R varies about ±15 % over −40°C to +85°C independent of size and rating; larger cases and higher ratings hold capacitance better under bias. DC bias, temperature and tolerance must be checked for each design.

The output current limits at 360 mA typical; past that the output voltage drops to hold the current constant. Above 150°C junction temperature the output turns off and comes back once the junction cools below 135°C. Into a hard short the part limits at 360 mA, heats to 150°C, shuts off, cools to 135°C and repeats, cycling between 360 mA and 0 mA as long as the short remains. For reliable operation the junction must be kept at or below 125°C.

Junction temperature is ambient plus dissipation times θJA, and θJA depends on the copper soldered to the GND pins. For a given ambient, headroom and load there is a minimum copper area that holds TJ at 125°C; the junction temperature curves give it per package. Where the board temperature is known, ΨJB gives the rise directly.

More copper on the pins carries more heat away, up to a point beyond which extra area gains little. The input capacitor belongs right at VIN and GND, the output capacitor right at VOUT and GND. 0805 or 1206 passives give the smallest footprint.
The input undervoltage lockout has a rising threshold of 2.69 V maximum, a falling threshold of 2.2 V minimum and 230 mV typical hysteresis.
